We have a close translation of the 1st tablet. It says "The Great Earth made herself glorious, her body flourished with greenery. Wide Earth put on silver metal and lapis lazuli ornaments, adorned herself with diorite, chalcedony, carnelian, and diamonds. The Visitor covered the pastures with irresistible sexual attraction, presented himself in majesty. The vast Visitor copulated with the wide Earth, seeding life into her womb. The Earth, for the happy birth of the Plants of Life and the Roots of Science, presented herself."

The second tablet defines magnetism long before William Gilbert observed the phenomenon using false scientific method. The Sumerians were told magnetic waves radiated outward from the Visitor's home deep in space and bounced their way from planet to planet, pulling them together into circular systems. Here on Earth, we see his Science clearly demonstrated. The Sumerians understood how to harness and alter these waves to enhance their lives. Why was this knowledge lost? How do we reclaim it?

In the third tablet, we're taught about a resonating device that allowed the Sumerians a window into alternate dimensions. While at first read, it sounds like a metaphor, the detailed Science behind the machine has been validated by New Dawn's own scientific experts. We know we could rebuild this device, but we are missing core energy components we believe are only found in space.

The fourth tablet explains our New Dawn. We are all remnants of the Visitor, unique in form, but collective in purpose. We are the Visitor's seeds, blossoming and reseeding, reaching towards the Heavens in a physical and spiritual path, until one day we advance enough to reach another world, and continue to spread into other galaxies. There is another story hidden within the text of the four tablets. Together, they speak of an end time, trillions of years in the future, where we will all be rejoined into the original form of the Visitor.

Once a bustling train station in Oakland, the 16th Street Station is now an historical landmark. It's being restored as part of a local redevelopment project.
Alameda Creek is a large stream in the Bay Area. It runs 45 miles and is the largest watershed in the southern San Francisco Bay.
The Blume Arena is an indoor arena in Oakland. It frequently hosts basketball games, concerts, and ice hockey games.

The Cathedral of Christ the Light in Oakland replaced the prior cathedral in the location after the Loma Prieta earthquake of 1989. This larger cathedral was built in the early 2000s, in an abstract and modern style.
Elmhurst is a large district in East Oakland, and remains one of the less expensive neighborhoods.
Woodland houses the largest Hispanic population within Oakland. It's named for the many orchards full of trees that dominated the area in the 1800s.
The Theater is one of Oakland's oldest still existing movie palaces, recently renamed to its new, simple moniker in a local fan contest. Second place was "Theater McTheaterface."

Jack London Square is a popular tourist destination, as well as providing entertainment and food for the locals. It's named after author Jack London and houses stores, hotels, and the relocated cabin Jack London once lived in.
Lakeside Park surrounds Lake Merritt, a large lagoon within Oakland. It became the United States' first official wildlife refuge back in the 1870s.
The North Hill neighborhood of Oakland is fully gentrified with a lower crime rate, higher household income, and few minority inhabitants than much of the rest of Oakland.
Oakland City Hall is the main seat of government within Oakland. It was the first high-rise government building in the United States. It was retrofitted after the Loma Prieta earthquake in 1989.
The Pacific Renaissance Plaza is a mix of residential, civic, and commercial space. It contains 50 affordable housing units out of 250 total. It also is the home of the Asian Branch of the library.
The Port of Oakland is a container ship facility. It's the 5th busiest container port in the United States, and was the first major port to accommodate container shipping.
The Prescott area of Oakland, also known as Lower Bottoms, has a history of higher rates of crime, gang activity, and poverty. It's currently going through the beginnings of gentrification.
Regwell Gun Range is one of the few remaining indoor/outdoor shooting ranges, and is therefore fairly popular.
Shoreline Park is on what used to be the Oakland Naval Supply Depot. It belongs to the Port of Oakland and is operated by the East Bay Regional Parks District.

The oil refinery employs 1,200+ workers and actively helped keep the local economy afloat during the Depression. It neighbors a now defunct explosives plant and the first neighborhood in California to sell to blacks.
Oakland Superior Court is the branch of the California Superior Court with jurisdiction over Oakland and the rest of Alameda County.
These are the main offices of social media giant !Nvite. They have a reputation for providing a fun workplace for their employees, no doubt to help attract top talent.
An infamous prison, known for being nearly impossible to escape. It figures prominently in many movies. The prison sits on an island just off San Francisco, surrounded by treacherous currents.
Nudle sponsored this popular baseball park as part of their move to contribute to the SF Bay Area community. It's gone over well with sports fans in particular.

Part of the Presidio, a former military base, Baker Beach lies in sight of the Golden Gate Bridge. It’s unofficially considered a nude beach. So, don't bring your bathing suit. Unless you really want to.
This bridge connects the City (what most non SF locals call San Francisco) with the East Bay. There’s a one way toll heading into the City, but it’s free to leave.
This illuminated and animated mural placed on grain silos is located at Pier 92 in the Port of San Francisco.
Once a popular movie palace, the Castro Theatre is now an historic landmark as well. It’s one of the last remaining movie palaces in the US. You can still catch film showings there today.
This is the oldest Chinatown in North America and contains the largest Chinese population outside of Asia. It is a popular tourist destination with its iconic Dragon Gate.
Just north of Market Street and Van Ness, the Civic Center has two large plazas that are home to government and cultural institutions. It's a National Historic Landmark, built in 1912.
The Cliff House is a well regarded restaurant with a famous view of the Bay. It's a popular location for tourists and locals, both.

Built to honor volunteer firefighter and inveterate gambler Lillie Hitchcock Coit, Coit Tower is a San Francisco landmark. Funding for the art deco tower came from Lillie’s bequest to the city upon her death in 1929.
Crestmont Forest is a popular location for hikers and equestrians. From nearby Sutro Hill, you can look out over the forest.

Embarcadero Center is a commercial complex of office buildings and hotels in the financial district of San Francisco. Dusk, Dawn, and Zombies was meant to be filmed here, but they were unable to get permits.

Built in 1898, the Ferry Building continues to serve as a ferry terminal. It hosts shops and restaurants focused on local products. The clock tower atop the building serves as one of San Francisco’s iconic structures.
Fisherman's Wharf is an incredibly popular tourist attraction. It contains the northern waterfront of San Francisco and is known for its restaurants, shops, and street performers.

Built just before the Civil War, the fort is now an historic site. It was never called upon to defend the Pacific Coast, although it was considered a key element of defense. It's located at the southern side of the Golden Gate bridge.
Ghirardelli Square contains shops and restaurants. It's a huge tourist location within Fisherman's Wharf as well as being an historic landmark.
The Golden Gate is the most famous bridge in the world. Spanning three miles between San Francisco and Marin, the bridge is considered one of the Wonders of the Modern World.
This is where HAUM collects and stores all the data from their smart houses.
Hook Motion Pictures is a local movie studio, currently working on what is anticipated to be an action blockbuster film starring Jimmy Siska.
Known colloquially as J Town, this neighborhood is the largest and oldest Japantown in the United States. It contains the famed Peace Pagoda as well as many other cultural landmarks.
Lombard Street is the steepest street in the city, with infamously awful hairpin turns. It’s an internationally known San Francisco landmark. Don’t get stuck driving on it if you can help it.
This popular park in the Mission District is quite close to The Castro and provides a view of the Mission, the Bay, downtown SF, and the East Bay.

Bordered by Chinatown, Fisherman’s Wharf, and Russian Hill, North Beach has a vibrant nightlife as well as residential housing. It was the center of the beatnik subculture and remains a vibrant neighborhood.

Ocean Beach is right next to Golden Gate Park. The water is known to have strong currents, which makes it popular with surfers and quite dangerous for swimmers. The water is generally cold and the weather often inclement.
These colorful Victorian houses are a famous SF landmark. The most famous street of them is just across from Alamo Square. They’ve also appeared in TV and movies.
Originally built to house artwork at the 1915 Panama-Pacific Exposition, the Palace of Fine Arts was one of the few expo structures to escape demolition. It's now a popular tourist spot.

One of the most popular shopping centers and tourist destinations in San Francisco, Pier 39 is at the edge of Fisherman’s Wharf. Visitors can see Alcatraz, the Golden Gate Bridge, and the famous Pier 39 sea lions.
This mountain sits across both San Francisco and San Bruno. Most of it is in the San Bruno Mountain State Park. As the highest point in the area, it has several radio broadcast towers.
This iconic TV and radio antenna has been part of the San Francisco skyline since 1973. They built the tall tower to provide signal that wouldn’t be disrupted by San Francisco’s many hills.
The Pyramid is the tallest skyscraper in San Francisco. It was built between 1969-1972. It has become a San Francisco icon thanks to it's unique silhouette.
This transit station in downtown San Francisco replaces the prior Transbay Terminal, which was damaged in the Loma Prieta earthquake. It connects 8 different counties.
The Twin Peaks are two hills near the center of San Francisco. The neighborhood surrounding them is also known as Twin Peaks, and was the location for a famous TV show.
Union Square refers to both the public square in the heart of downtown San Francisco and the shopping, hotel, and theater district surrounding the plaza.
Vermont Street may well be the crookedest street in the world, beating out notoriously steep Lombard Street. In fact, it's steeper than Lombard. Both are major traffic zones.
No one is quite sure what goes on behind the walls of the Spiritual Ascendance Development Facility. This religious group is often viewed with suspicion and considered a cult.
WKZ is the local TV news station. They’re always glad to provide sensational stories and are often a source of controversy within the community.
Horseshoe Bay is a popular tourist destination within Marin. It once was home to an army outpost. The soldiers have relocated, but the buildings remain. Some repurposed as luxury hotels.
Considered a national park within the Marin headlands, this scenic area is a favorite for tourists and campers. It sits just north of the Golden Gate Bridge.

The Point Bonita Lighthouse stands in the Marin Headlands, providing guidance for ships in the San Francisco Bay. It was the first lighthouse to have a fog signal and the last manned lighthouse in California.
The other bridge to North Bay. This bridge crosses between the East Bay (Oakland) up to Marin. Often less crowded than the Golden Gate.
This affluent city is part of Marin County. It was originally a shipbuilding center during WWII. These days it's a tourist destination with beautiful scenery and houseboats.
The Gates Houseboats have been here since the 1950s, providing places for bohemians and hippies to live off grid. Local residents and law enforcement aren't so fond of the boats.
Arguably the best vantage point to get a photo of the Golden Gate Bridge and San Francisco. No trip to San Francisco is complete without getting a shot at Vista Point.
Rhonda’s Restaurant is surrounded by nature and plays host to Silicon Valley entrepreneurs, families, hikers, tourists, musicians and more. The food is locally sourced and the atmosphere is homey.
Crystal Springs Dam is a gravity dam in San Mateo. It was one of the first gravity dams built in the US, in 1888. It's survived both major earthquakes to hit the Bay Area since that time.

The Dumbarton Bridge connects the Peninsula to the East Bay. It's the southernmost bridge in the Bay Area, with ends in Fremont and Menlo Park. It's free to go to the East Bay, but there's a toll the other direction.
El Camino Real Station was once the hub of the Silicon Valley mass transit system. These days it's been replaced by a more modern station, but the original remains as an historic landmark.
Fury Track is an abandoned race track in Silicon Valley, best known for a scandal 10 years ago when an announcer streaked across the track during live broadcast.
Galilei is an aerospace manufacturer specializing in space exploration and transport. They are particularly known for their communication satellites.
Swan Leavitt Observatory is a radio telescope in the foothills by Stanford. The giant telescope was funded by the US Air Force in the 1960s.
Built in the days of Eichler and Frank Lloyd Wright, this modern church now belongs to the New Dawn. Though rumors abound regarding the religious group, the temple remains an architectural landmark.
Nudle is one of the largest employers in Silicon Valley these days. The relatively young company has made tremendous strides since it was founded.
Palo Alto is at the heart of Silicon Valley. It's an affluent area with housing prices easily over the million mark. It's also the home of Stanford University.
The St. Gianna Salt Farm is remarkably beautiful, particularly from an aerial view. The various different bodies of water have differing colors depending on their mineral and biological content.
There's San Mateo the city and San Mateo the county (which contains the city as well as much of the rest of Silicon Valley). San Mateo city is at the northmost end of Silicon Valley.
Stanford is often referred to as the West Coast Ivy League. It's a prestigious school located in Palo Alto, giving its students access to Silicon Valley.
The Storm Drain is the central joining point of a series of canals underlying San Mateo. Rumors abound that various gangs have used them as hideouts in the past. Possibly even now.
Tidis has been around since the early days of Silicon Valley. They've weathered ups and downs, and lasted through booms and busts.

All of us have probably stared up at the peaceful, starlit sky and wondered if we'll make some new friends out there within our own lifetime, right? And how would we do that? Rockets. But the sad truth is that for every advancement mankind has made in space exploration, we've seen the same technology used for violence. We don't know who invented the first rocket, but it likely comes soon after the invention of gunpowder. And we all know where gunpowder went. Guns. Cannonballs. Rocket-propelled projectiles.

Fireworks, yes. And that's a good counterpoint. Fireworks bring people together to celebrate, right? The science of "let's ignite something to make something else hurl forward at breakneck speed" is an old one, but it wasn't until 1926 that a man named Robert Goddard invented the first liquid-fuelled rocket and the modern rockets-aimed-towards-space era really kicked off. Of course as we made huge advancements with that goal, the war machine was keeping up. Bigger and bigger propelled weapons of destruction. Bigger payloads. At Galelei, we have a pretty simple goal. We'd like to use rockets to get up there and advance mankind towards something peaceful, something all nations can work together to accomplish, before we wipe ourselves out with that other kind of rocket.

My first time out with the Sons is both exciting and disappointing. I’m expecting madness. Growling and howling into the wind while claiming the highways and leaving a path of destruction behind the massive metal beasts we ride on. There’s some growling and howling at first, but mostly it’s just riding fast, lanesplitting. These are no madmen owning the freeways. They take me to a bar, just like any other motorcycle bar. Machines lined up outside, like dominoes that would all fall over if you were to tip one. Not that anyone would. There are always a few Sons on guard, rotating out as the night passes. You can see the military training that many of these men share. Inside the bar is dark, with a genuine jukebox. Who still uses jukeboxes in these days, when mp3 players are ubiquitous and cheap? “What do you think?” my guide asks me, and I can already tell he’s expecting me to be impressed. To be intimidated by their fierceness. “Eh,” I say. “It’s kind of tame.” He frowns and I wonder for a moment if he’s going to punch me, to prove to me the folly of my words.“You ever been out on the front lines?” he asks me instead, which surprises me. “A time or two,” I tell him. It is, after all, how I made my name. “Then you know,” he says. “The fighting? The explosions and the blood and the gunshots? That’s only part of the time. 20 percent, maybe. Most of the time is waiting and planning. What I’m saying,” he continues, “is the exciting stuff? That happens. But we’re not just gangbangers. We’re soldiers. Fighters. Have been from the start.”

Of them all, the Bratva have been most resistant to letting me in. There’s something old world about them, almost stately—at least about the ones at the top of the food chain. The boys at the bottom are flunkies like any others. They aspire to power, though. You can see it. The Bratva know their history, they know where they’re from. And they know where they’re going. They are not happy with me. An older man with a thick Russian accent glares at me. He ought to be smoking a cigar, to complete the scene, but he isn’t. He has a drink, but it’s just water. “You,” he says, “you are in a risky business, my friend.” “Am I your friend?” I ask, even though I know it’s a stupid question. “You cozy up vith Aryan pigs. Ve see you Vith the latinos, too. And the Chinese boys. Tell me vhy, little boy, I vould even vant to keep you alive?” I knew I should have saved the Sons for last. With their anti-semitism, it’s no wonder they’re not popular with my current host. The Bratva have a long history of hiding within Jewish immigrant populations. “I’m just a reporter,” I tell the man. “Looking for something interesting to write.” He barks out a laugh. “Oh, interesting. Interesting ve certainly have. But ve will not be sharing our history vith you or anyvone. Too many bodies, and the Bratva know vhere they’re buried.” There’s something chilling about the way he says it that makes me realize for the first time I could get myself killed doing this. The Sons I thought might beat me up. The Tezcas would threaten me, but liked having an audience too much to really hurt me. Auntie Shu’s boys were damn near inscrutable, but still, I wasn’t worried. Not truly. This man… he’d be perfectly happy killing me and no one would ever find my body.

“Why the hell should I take you anywhere?” the woman says to me, dark eyes surveying me from head to toe. Whatever she sees doesn’t impress her, clearly. “I’m a reporter-“ I start to say. “Who gives a fuck?” she asks. “Reporters don’t know shit.” “I’m writing about the gangs in the Bay Area,” I continue, keeping my voice calm. She shakes her head at me. “Crazy.” “No one ever gets to hear from the real people,” I tell her, beginning to get a sense of how I might persuade her. “All anyone knows is what the news anchors on TV tell them. And you and I both know how realistic that is.” She snorts in agreement, and at that moment I know I’ve hooked her. She tells me to call her Lus Amanda. “Is that your real name?” I ask. She just laughs. And so starts my time with the Tezcas. My guide grew up in Los Angeles, I learn, as did many of the other gang members. Their move to the Bay Area is fairly recent, and they’re still carving out their chunk of flesh. Piss them off, and they’ll gladly stick a knife between your ribs. Lus Amanda tells me she killed her first man when she was 13, and then smiles, like a shark showing off her pearly whites. My Spanish, which up until now I’d been quite proud of, barely serves me at all. The way they speak, the swiftness of it, the lilt, the accent… is nothing like my schoolboy Spanish. I need to unlearn what I know, or treat their speech like an entirely different language.

“Man’s one hard headed mother-fucker,” Chuck Z tells me, shaking out the fingers of his right hand. [He’d just punched the man in question in the face, so I guess he’d know just how hard-headed the guy was]. “What’d he do, anyway?” I ask, watching as two of Chuck’s boys drag the bleeding man away. Chuck shrugs. “Talked some smack, then tried to go indie.” Going indie. Going independent. One of the cardinal sins for any member of the 580s. Going independent means trying to leave their extensive drug distribution network. It’s a lucrative racket, if you can cut it and keep the 580s from catching you. The 580s take a chunk of the profits, but they also make sure to keep all their dealers well supplied and protected. Anyone tries to hurt a 580 dealer, they don’t last long. And somehow charges just don’t stick to anyone the cops pick up. Not that they pick up many. Clearly, there’s a lot of money passing hands. Considering the tithes the 580s require, I can see how going independent might be tempting. Of course, considering the way our erstwhile friend looks by the time Chuck’s boys are done with him, the temptation isn’t that big. It’s his first offense, so they let him live. Chuck himself wouldn’t look out of place in any start-up boardroom in Silicon Valley--aside from being black. He’s well dressed, wearing designer jeans and a leather jacket I know goes for nearly a thousand dollars. He wears a thick gold ring on his right hand. The man has money, and he wants people to know it.

Umeni-Zulu are quite clear on one thing — they are not a gang. They are private military contractors. Regardless, you can’t look at the gang scene in the Bay Area without taking their presence into account. In addition to experience, and utter ruthlessness, they also have cutting edge tech and friends in high places. Very high places. They also have more experience dealing with reporters than any of the other groups I’ve been tracking. My contact narrows his eyes at me. “You want to know how Umeni-Zulu works? Fine. Three rules: One, we tell you to keep something quiet, you keep it quiet. Two, you get in our way on an op, it's your funeral. Three, we get final say on what you write about us.” “As a journalist…” I begin. “As a human,” he interrupts, “if you want to stay alive, you do it our way. Or you don’t get your ride-along with us. Got it?” Pretty clear. “Got it,” I say, and then mutter, “hardass.” "What's that?" he says, ready to pounce. "Nothing," I say. "Just taking notes."

Right now, I'm sitting at the counter at a hole-in-the-wall noodle shop, although it feels more like I'm in someone's kitchen. The elderly shop owner sets a bowl of noodles with sliced pork in front of me. Next to me, a young man--almost a boy--receives the same meal. He says something in Cantonese to the owner. This young man, Chan, is a member of the Auntie Shu boys. "Eat," he tells me. I do, but I'm wondering when he's going to actually show me anything interesting. "You think I just want to feed you?" he scoffs. "This is one of our shops. Tang opened it when he was too old for street work." When we leave, the owner hands Chan a bag. "What's that?" I ask. Chan looks at me like I must be the worst kind of idiot and shakes his head. "Come on," he says, "next shop." And I realize, I really am dense. This is part of Auntie Shu's extensive money laundering operation. We stop by a grocery, a drycleaners, and several more restaurants before Chan decides we're done. Are the Auntie Shu boys trying to come across as harmless? Well done, mon ami! You have won a race against some of San Francisco's most wealthy and influential people!

Three... I could see a Predator spearmaster keeping two away with a Yautja combistick, but a third xeno's going to be able to get in close. Even if he kills it, that blood splash is going to melt right through him. It's a hard call. You'd have to plug their stats into a probability algorithm.
They've both fought Judge Dredd. Which is pretty badass. Aliens fought Batman.

Can't remember. Doesn't matter. You know what... I give the overall win to Predator.

Lay your secrets bare for true freedom!

Man, Sitara hates it when I fuck with Josh, but he makes it too easy sometimes. I told him that New Dawn was looking to brainwash socially awkward hackers into their secret army. A mindless drone army to overthrow the government. It's got him all freaked out!
Yeah, yeah. I know... but you should have seen his face. I wouldn't do it if he didn't make it so rewarding! Ok.. I'll tell him I made it up. Promise.
I wish I could see what's under the hood of that car they're using for the CyberDriver movie.

Now that we're clear, you can drop me off.

No limit on this operation’s budget. The equipment here is top shelf.

He helped me put together the controller-board for the drone. I had all the diodes in upside down. He laughed about that for weeks.

I didn't know Horatio much, but I've had friends go down in hard circumstances. It's tough. It's always tough, no matter what. You can't get around it, just gotta fight through it and do what you can that's best by Horatio.
We're getting close now. This is going to be huge. How does it feel, man?
Half the time, I can't tell if shit is Darwin Award level stupidity or some asshole's idea of a marketing stunt.
This shit with !Nvite. I don't like feeling used, Marcus. It makes me want to take a sledgehammer to limbs and jumper cables to soft body parts.

They mentioned a safe house. Do me a favor, analyze the GPS data on the phones of all these people.
See if there's a place they visit regularly.

I'll mark it on your map.

Try to keep it speedy, Marcus. They've got the HaDoCk trap all set and ready to go.
There’s a whole doc of code names!
You found a code name back at the boat house of the guy that HaDoCk warned to go off the grid.
Looking, looking. Here it is, Redbeard! Real name: Lovro Tomic.
That guy's not going to find HaDoCk anytime soon.
Maybe. Check out this email I just got.
I take that to mean we’re out of the HaDoCk doghouse.

The tough exterior that conceals my secretly vulnerable heart.

She's been selling Zero Day exploits for years. And now with her Prime_Eight posse working with gangs... [hesitates] We're starting to take a lot of big risks. This isn't what most of us signed up for.

Any ideas on what kind of encryption they're using?
I'm going to take a closer look and see what low-grade shit they're running.

What the hell? This is gang territory. HaDoCk's working with gangs now?
No. HaDoCk wouldn't work with gangs.
Because the alternative doesn't make any sense. He wouldn't.
I'm hoping I can grab their GPS data and figure out where they took him.

The reality, when you're dealing with things like radiation and space dust, is you're going to want as much shielding between you and the ship's exterior as you can get. Imagine how that will look. Visit a Motocross Race [ACTIVITY_BIKE] location to engage in off-road motocross trials in and around San Francisco.
• Gain followers [FOLLOWERS] and money [MONEY] based on performance and track difficulty.

Visit a Sailboat Race [ACTIVITY_SAILING] location to engage in sailing competitions around San Francisco Bay.

Visit a Drone Race [ACTIVITY_DRONE] location to engage in a flying drone trial on neon-lit tracks around San Francisco.
• Beat the time-trial marks and win a gold, silver, or bronze medal! • Gain followers [FOLLOWERS] and money [MONEY] based on performance and track difficulty.

Playstyles are the different ways hackers can approach situations. It's common to mix it up depending on the situation.
• "Ghost" hackers rely on [CSS_TUTO_RED]stealth and subterfuge[CSS_END] to reach their goal and avoid confrontation. • "Trickster" hackers are masters of [CSS_TUTO_RED]remote control devices[CSS_END]. They complete operations without ever endangering themselves. • "Aggressor" hackers use a very [CSS_TUTO_RED]hands-on[CSS_END] approach and attack problems head-on.

The "Ghost" hacker puts utmost importance on DedSec being an invisible force - get in, get it done, get out before they ever knew you were there.
• Tools of choice are the stun gun and other suppressed weapons. • Skills that create [CSS_TUTO_RED]distractions[CSS_END] should be prioritized.

The "Trickster" hacker is all about manipulation - have fun doing what needs to be done, and do it with panache.
• Invest in the Jumper and Quadcopter, available at any hackerspace's 3D printer. • Skills that allow you to [CSS_TUTO_RED]manipulate objects[CSS_END] and [CSS_TUTO_RED]remote-controlled devices[CSS_END] should be prioritized.

The "Aggressor" hacker thinks DedSec should be a force to be reckoned with, going in with a bang. They hit hard and leave nothing behind.
• Invest in the weapons available at any hackerspace's 3D printer. • Skills that improve [CSS_TUTO_RED]marksmanship[CSS_END] and [CSS_TUTO_RED]throwable gadgets[CSS_END] are preferred.

The subject is remarkable in that he wears a mask at all times. The mask prevents our facial recognition software from determining his identity. We have also run several vocal passes, the results are indeterminate as to region and upbringing. His work is that of a high-level, albeit self-taught, hacker whose calling card often involves crude jokes left encoded into his target's core program.

Previous to his DedSec involvement, the subject known as Wrench mostly pursued cyber-attacks of dubious humoristic value. Changing website text to scatalogical verbiage, often using bathroom humor. This sort of adolescent acting-out has transformed as he has become more deeply involved in DedSec. He now operates within a team, generally pursuing either corporate or political targets. The subject is considered dangerous.

As for DedSec member Wrench. Surveillance indicates that he is awkward around the opposite sex and uses his mask as a deflecting device. A psych analysis postulates a disrupted childhood along with possible debilitating shyness. Subject copes with this using a mask which he has programmed to reflect his emotions as a sort of electronic billboard. Within the world in which the subject operates, this solution is considered ingenious.

!Nvite's terms of service allow us to direct the news and social content of our users' feeds without their knowledge in order to better our business. The first of these "emotional contagion" tests spanned three months. Our client selections were based on political leaning, emotional stability rating, and amount of social contacts. The phase one goal was to see how easily we could shift the emotional state and post content of the least stable users. The results were astounding--a 96% success rate. By bombarding their feeds with negative news, content that questioned their world views, and reminders of moments shared with loved ones (divorced or deceased), we were able to generate feeds full of negative posts from our subjects. We had effectively changed their moods. To solidify our results, we were able to "reset" their emotional states by refilling their feeds with positive news and reminders.

Phase 2 of !Nvite's emotional contagion testing presented a bigger challenge to us. our goal was to take more business-focused user, those with less social media interaction, and attempt to shift their emotional profiles. Altering their news feeds and social reminders had little impact as they primarily use !Nvite to promote their products. So, we took a different approach. We focused on their businesses. Suggested sites and recommended articles were custom tailored to each client, showing promotional material from their more successful competitors. We also focused on links to stories about major failures and bankruptcy in the client's field of work. While we saw no real change in post content, we saw clear impacts on their businesses - price drops, investment in training, and even layoffs.

I take no joy in this report because I believe my colleagues are decent cops, but I've seen enough this week to convince me we have a storm brewing. I don't know how the software is consistently getting it wrong, but I advise suspending its use until we can work out the glitches.

Unfortunately, I'm going to have to ask for a transfer back to the DPD. I feel my career, and even my safety, will be at risk if I keep running with my current unit. People often ask me why I put so much time and energy into pushing out there into space when it's so far and so empty. Let's look at just our own little space-pebble. It would take us lifetimes to experience all the culture, all the color of our planet, but we do feel like we have a pretty good handle on it at least. It's getting harder and harder to really surprise us with anything. I absolutely believe there are other planets just as teeming with life out there for us to find. We're taking a look at the collected public reactions to our three Watcher robot prototypes. Our test run with the faceless robot resulted in very little public interaction. In fact, many people altered their paths to the other side of the street to avoid the machine. A few key comments we collected were, "I didn't understand what it was doing," "It looks like a weapon," and "It's totally a killbot." In hindsight, the red recording light does come across as a bit military.
That's right. You can come pick it up whenever you're ready.

It's separate, but I can give you a friends and family discount on it, since you're purchasing something custom.
Do you have studded ones? Or ones modeled on fruits?
We have a variety of styles, whatever suits your needs. You tell us, we'll hunt it down.
You guys are the best. I can't wait!

The Watcher robot used in our second field test was wearing the "gentleman" face with additional eyebrow panels and a more comical paint scheme. We knew he would score better with people on the street, but we hadn't anticipated such a strong reaction. In fact, the machine could not perform its patrol due to the amount of people trying to stop it, pose with it, and take photos. Some of the feedback included, "he's so British!," "I want to adopt him," and "his eyebrows are too sarcastic." We recommend halting development in this direction unless Tidis intends to branch into the amusement industry.

The third Watcher robot field test was equipped with a more human-shaped prosthetic head capable of mimicking human mouth movements and the ability to "look" at nearby people with its realistic eyes. The test was an absolute failure. We'll use one of the responses we collected on the street to sum up our recommendation for this direction: "Drop this thing in a hole and set it on fire."

I've been asked to provide the board with an update on Blume's "people of interest," where they are, what measures we're taking to prevent further damages, and what we should expect in the future. Thanks to Mr. Pearce, a lot of our sensitive data was leaked and our PR department was forced into overdrive, causing us to push ctOS 2.0 years before it was ready.

Mr. Pearce caused plenty of physical damage as well, shooting up several of our installations, infecting the ctOS with a custom virus, and blacking out Chicago itself. The good news--we've reset, refocused, and we are back on target. But what threat does Mr. Pearce still pose? As far as we can tell, we were only a target of opportunity during his criminal rampage and we believe we're off his radar for the time being. We don't fully understand his agenda.

The second thorn in Blume's side is no stranger to most of us... Mr. Raymond Kenney. Though Kenney was a ctOS pioneer, he was also a whistleblower who decided to turn on his own team. He was unsuccessful. His response took out the Northeast power grid, leaving 11 people dead. Collateral damage. Kenney went underground soon after and although we've been working very closely with law enforcement, he has remained one step ahead of us ever since. We almost caught him in Pawnee, Illinois where he posed as a sculptor named "T-Bone," to set up camp near one of our main offices. He gave us the slip.

Raymond Kenney's primary goal seems to be an end to our company, which leads us to believe he is mentally unstable. Indeed, he has often allied with other troubled minds, including Aiden Pearce and another former Blume engineer, Tobias Frewer. We believe Kenney is an active threat and we expect he will try to attack ctOS 2.0.
What do you make of these hacktivists?

Let's talk about Blume's current elephant in the room. DedSec. Last year, if you had told me I'd be doing a risk assessment on these jokers, I would have laughed. But here's the reality... their numbers have grown exponentially. They've got public sentiment on their side--in fact, many unaffiliated people help them out by donating processing power by distributing their messages. What started as a relatively harmless group of pranksters has turned into a movement.

We see these fads come and go. Activists and rebels drawing in mainstream support and surging for a summer. They tend to fade away as people lose interest. Our problem - people aren't losing interest. We've seen several of our partners taking big hits from these hackers. They keep getting win after win and there's no sign of that momentum slowing. Their message seems to be anti-big business and anti-establishment, which puts our company and its products firmly into their warped perception of "bad guy" territory.
What the fuck is a hactivist?
Anarchists, mostly. Some kind of scriptkiddies who want to play vigilante.

I guess? All the execs and shareholders are concerned about us securing neighborhoods if things go sideways.

Keep in mind Kenney is a master manipulator, operates at a high level of expertise, and has extensive knowledge about our company. Our own employees have been tricked into letting him through our doors on multiple occasions. The current plan for dealing with Raymond Kenney is to have a proper response waiting for him, because he will strike again. You'll note we recently sent pictures of him in the employee newsletter to try to build awareness.

They will attack us and it's going to be soon. They will have a lot of public support on their side. We need to be extra secure with our data, careful to avoid any PR blunders that could attract more people to their cause, and to be extra vigilant with our secure assets. If we're lucky, DedSec's going to do something to turn the public against them, effectively robbing them of their most important resource - supporters.

Remember the 90s? How it felt to escape those secluded BBS's and join *The Internet*? What a utopia it was, where knowledge and culture could be exchanged freely, regardless of social and geographical boundaries. I remember those early days. I remember them very well. We dreamed of direct democracy and enlightenment of the human race, and in our hands, we held the tool to take us there. Those days are long behind us now.

Try to imagine the world without internet. Think about how boring computers must have been back then. Believe it or not, but the greatest hackers ever came from that era. We had no way to have fun with a computer but to try and understand how it worked, what made it tick and tock. We hackers are at our best when we're fighting boredom. The day we stop fighting, we become managers.

Open your eyes. It started with “responsible disclosure” but they wanted more control, more Zero Days. Now the military-industrial complex has its eye on cyber, and the big weapon companies want us to disappear. They organize to shut us down through arrangements like the Wassenaaar. They want to be the only Zero Day dealers. We're seen as the enemy, but who else will protect the people's privacy? Who else will keep the internet free? If we don't fight back, we will vanish, and so will our culture.

So. DedSec. If nothing else, it's refreshing to see some hacktivists who know a thing or two about tech; not just launching an LOIC to DDoS the outrage du jour. Shame they're such flamboyant fucking hipsters. The best hackers are the ones who stay hidden. That’s always been the case. But goddamn, watching them put society's nose in its own shit is fun as hell.

"Making the world a better place." The verbal opiate we're fed day in, day out. Cut to modern-day San Francisco, a hivemind of techbros whose only career plan is an IPO, living in houses that nobody can afford, strangling diversity like a babe in its crib. That's the world Big Data wants. That's what they consider "a better place." The only comfort I find is in knowing we'll either blow ourselves up or kill the planet before that ever happens.

Question: why are we so capable of amazing things as individuals, but fail so miserably when we work en masse? Huxley and Orwell both wrote of dystopian futures, one driven by a neverending flow of entertainment, the other by an unblinking eye. Not only did we ignore them but we managed to wrap BOTH dystopias into one! Huxley hit the nail on the head, but Orwell didn't. Big Brother doesn't need to put cameras in our faces. We do it ourselves! It's the idea of NOT being watched that scares us now. Chew on that, Georgie.

Do you remember the early 90s, when we escaped those secluded BBSs and joined the “internet”? We were all dreaming of a true techno utopia. An open place where all knowledge could be gained, enriching conversations had with ANYONE, without social boundaries... We even cheered the cyber-independence of internet when it was released. I remember, very well. We were dreaming of direct democracy and enlightenment for the entire human race. It was the most promising tool ever created, and it was for us, all of us. And look what we've done with it.

There was a time, I tell you, when the internet didn't exist. Do you realize how boring a computer was in those days? You probably have no idea, but trust me - this is what created made the most amazing hackers history has ever seen. If you wanted to have fun with a computer you had no choice but to try and understand how it worked, what made it tick and tock and spit out errors. Hackers are at their best - their most creative! - when they're fighting against boredom. The day they stop fighting it? They become managers.

These aren’t your friends! Not real ones, at any rate. Not people you actually want to spend time with, have a beer with. They are bullshit people from high school who you don't know anything about anymore! The tech companies have turned your phone into a slot machine. When you check it, maybe you’ll get a hit. And they make you follow people you don’t know and Like things you don’t care about because you’re afraid of digital ostracization!
No, no, not you. You’re strong. If you’re so strong, give me your phone for the rest of the day.
See what I mean? These companies are evil, and only DedSec is calling them out for it!
Those DedSec members. They’re like a fanatical cult.
The real criminals are those who are stealing our privacy and using our personal information against us.

No… the real criminals are the goons who claim they oppose violence but break into research companies and cause tens of thousands of dollars in damage. Who claim they want people to vote, but then screw with the results. Who say they want ‘no more lies’ but hide their faces? Who say they want to protect us but are responsible for how much gun violence?

Uh, what? Are you getting all your news from WKZ and talk radio again? What you said doesn’t even make any sense. DedSec are the ones giving a voice to the voiceless and yeah, maybe they have to stand up for what they believe in. That makes them heroes to me.

Do you see? Do you see what’s happening? It's right in front of your face. It started with “responsible disclosure,” but they wanted more control, and more Zero Days. Now that the big weapon companies are into cyber-everything they want us to disappear. They lobby governments to shut us down through arrangements like the Wassenaar[WASH-en-are]. They want to be the only ones dealing in Zero Days. It makes sense. Without us, who will fix internet? Who will warn users about institutional surveillance or, at the most basic level, protect people’s security? Their privacy? Unless we fight - together - we're going to disappear. Just like those big companies want.

Not sure what to think about those DedSec cats. On one hand, it’s refreshing to see some hacktivists that know a thing or two about tech, not just launching LOIC to DDOS the fresh new hate of the day. But on the other hand, their flamboyance and hipsterism is nauseating. The best hackers are the ones we’ve never heard of. That’s how it's always been, and that’s how it should be. But hell if watching them stick all those CISO's noses in their own shit is not an amazing form of entertainment.

If I hear ANYONE in Silicon Valley saying “we’re making the world a better place” and it doesn't come from some amped up, Pied Piper employee’s mouth, I tell you, I am going to go on a rampage. Just look at what they've done to the city! You've got a predominantly young male techbro population whose only career plan ends in an IPO, who pay thousands to price out the working class from their own neighborhoods, and then you top it off with a millionaire, herd-like mentality. Who thought that was a model for success? I mean, hey, if it’s about making the whole world this kind of a "better place," the Big One can’t come too soon!

Sometimes I wonder why we, as a species, can be so amazing individually but fail so hard when it comes to the masses. Huxley and Orwell both wrote about dystopian futures, one driven by a never-ending flow of entertainment, the other by a technological Eye of Sauron. Not only did we not listen, but we settled for BOTH as our current dystopia. While I still can’t fault Huxley’s approach, Orwell failed badly. No need for Big Brother to put cameras in our living rooms when we buy them ourselves. Not only that, our biggest concern isn't privacy, or people hacking into our homes. It's that, even if our feeds DID go live, nobody would watch them!

The cells inside Alcatraz are 5 feet by 9 feet, and 7 feet high. There are 336 cells in B & C blocks combined, but each cell contained only a single prisoner. Some inmates, such as Willie Radkay, considered the privacy afforded by this arrangement to be a great advantage over other federal institutions of the time, while others likened the imprisonment to feeling like, "a cockroach feels in a matchbox."

D Block is where the solitary confinement cells were located. These 6 rooms were collectively referred to as "the Hole." Here, some prisoners were locked in a darkness so complete it caused visual and auditory hallucinations. Other prisoners in D Block were let out of their cells only once a week, to enter the rec[recreation] yard, alone, for an hour before returning to their cells.

The Mess Hall is where the staff and those prisoners not in solitary confinement would eat their meals. The ceiling was rigged with tear gas canisters, and the entry housed a metal detector. At the end of each 20-minute meal, all of the forks, spoons, and knives would be laid out on the table and carefully counted to ensure that none of the inmates had managed to smuggle away a potential weapon.

On May 2nd, 1946, the Battle of Alcatraz began. Two inmates, Bernard Coy and Marvin Hubbard, overpowered William Miller and locked him in one of the cells. Coy, who had been starving himself, was then able to force himself through the bars protecting the gun gallery and take command of the prison from within. By the time the failed escape attempt was resolved, forty-four hours later, 2 guards and 3 prisoners were dead.

The Alamo Square shoe garden started as a way to protect saplings with discarded shoes, but quickly became a whimsical garden with shoes serving as plant pots. There are some environmental concerns.
These colorful Victorian houses were built in the late 1800s. Also known as postcard row, the houses have come to represent San Francisco and can be spotted in countless movies and television series.

The Bay Bridge connects San Francisco to Oakland and the rest of the East Bay. There’s a toll entering SF, though not leaving. The bridge was famously damaged during the Loma Prieta Eathquake in 1989.
Named for Captain George J. Godfrey, this gun battery was installed in San Francisco in 1896. It was deactivated as obsolete in 1942. Today it’s part of the Golden Gate Recreation Area.
This battery was named for Maj. Gen. Joseph Spencer, a Revolutionary War hero who died 100 years prior. The battery was placed in Marin County in 1897 and deactivated as obsolete in 1942.

In 2013, Chicago realized the promise of smart cities with ctOS, [Silence 0.5]a citywide operating system merging big data with surveillance, security, and transit programs.

With a few hundred lines of code, hackers were able to hijack its central servers and cripple the entire grid. [Silence 0.1]Many believed the attack would be a killing blow for smart city development. [Silence 0.1]They were wrong.

Coordinated from the heart of Silicon Valley, ctOS 2.0 has been implemented across the United States, ushering in the “Internet of Things”. [Silence 0.1]6.4 billion connected devices now serve as collection points, [Silence 0.1]mapping and recording our daily routines, [Silence 0.1]making a more secure...and more invasive system. [Silence 0.1]But who else is listening?

Big Brother no longer works alone. [Silence 0.1]Thousands of little brothers monitor and aggregate your every move, building a complete digital profile of YOU, to be bought, sold or stolen in an instant.

Insurance companies use algorithms to monitor your life habits [Silence 0.1]and limit or deny coverage. [Silence 0.1]Health providers determine if your cancer is worth treating. [Silence 0.1]Search results and news feeds are skewed to bias mood [Silence 0.1]and influence your vote, engineering social uprisings on a massive scale. [Silence 0.1]You are now less valuable than the data you produce. [Silence 0.1]This is the new reality. [Silence 0.1]Going dark is no longer an option.

With threats to personal freedom rising, many are stepping forward. [Silence 0.1]Whistleblowers, Activists and Hackers have drawn their battle lines, [Silence 0.1]putting the establishment on watch. [Silence 0.1]But are they threats themselves... [Silence 0.1]or have they become freedom’s last line of defense?

Once a rank is attained in the Leaderboard app, it cannot be lost until the season ends.
People's profiles contain various tidbits about their lives such as hobby and occupation. It even shows their current mood!
Some civilians have peculiar personalities and some of them even carry weapons… Be vigilant!
The Engine Override research allows you to use a burst of speed while driving by pressing [NITRO] at the cost of Botnet Resources.
You can control the angle of your vehicle mid-air with [AIRCONTROL] to stick the landing!
Went a little overboard and flipped your vehicle? Don't worry, you can flip it back on its wheels by using [NAVIGATION]!
Sports cars allow you to perform quick maneuvers which is ideal to escape pursuers in back alleys.
Off-road driving is challenging with most vehicles. Try an off-road truck or a dirt bike when using non-paved roads!
Muscle cars are built to last. Don't hesitate to engage in car combat while driving them.
Performance vehicles will make you the king of the highway, or any other long, straight road.
Steampipes allow you to blow up the ground beneath fleeing targets or pursuers in spectacular ways.
Restricted Areas are off-limits. Getting spotted inside one will result in your arrest.
If you're spotted in a Restricted Area and you don't move, enemies will attempt to arrest you. If you move, they will open fire!
When you are being detected, a white circular arrow appears on the screen. If it's not filled, you can still hide!
Calling the police [HACK_POLICESEARCH] on enemies with the APB research hack is a great way to remove the attention from yourself!
Calling a gang with the Gang Attack research hack is useful to eliminate a target and create chaos!
Explosive devices or any kind of environmental explosions are the most effective solutions against an armored enemy.
Hacking Invasion: As a target, use proximity trigger hacks [HACK_PROXIMITY] to trap unsuspecting hackers!
Hacking Invasion: As a target, it's possible to reveal the presence of the hacker by hacking the vehicle they're in!
Bounty Hunter: As a hunter, you can stop the target from escaping by hacking their vehicle.
Bounty Hunter: As a hunter, you'll get points even if you're not the one who kills the target, but dealing the final blow gives increased rewards.
Bounty Hunter: As a target, eliminate bounty hunters to earn more rewards!
If your wanted level [FELONY_HEAT] is over 3, there's a chance that Bounty Hunters will appear and hunt you down!
COOP: Use the Quadcopter and the attract hack [HACK_ATTRACT] to create opportunities for your online partner!
When your objective is purple, it means you are playing Online and other players can show up!
If your vehicle is getting hacked by an online player, it's possible to fight back against the hack and stay on course.
You can find civilian "talkers" all around San Francisco. They'll tell you more about the world they live in!
The Hackerspace in San Francisco is where DedSec plans their operations. More will appear as you progress through the game!
Look out for collectibles, like paint jobs [COLLECTIBLE_PAINTJOB], unique vehicles [COLLECTIBLE_VEHICLE] and clothing [COLLECTIBLE_CLOTH], while roaming the city.
Short on cash? Find money bags [COLLECTIBLE_SPORTBAG] around the world for large cash rewards or partake in world activities!
While in NetHack, Research Points [RESEARCHPOINT] and Key Data [KEYDATA] emit a blue signal that makes them easier to find!
Accumulate followers [FOLLOWERS] to gain new Research Points [RESEARCHPOINT] and unlock new Operations for the DedSec App!
While in NetHack, hidden Operations emit an orange signal that makes them easier to find!

The original Chicago DedSec has coordinated operations, everybody mostly working towards the same goal. [Silence 0.1]Rumors say that the "leaderless" group actually has somebody upstairs calling the shots--the "Council of Daves." [Silence 0.1]I can't say if that's true or not, but somebody's focusing their efforts. [Silence 0.1]I know because I studied everything about them, even ran with a few of their ops. [Silence 0.1]I wanted to emulate them. Tried to figure out what worked and applied it to us. [Silence 0.1]But the members of our Bay Area DedSec couldn't be more different from each other.

DedSec found Josh... Hawt Sauce... [Silence 0.5]posting anti-ctOS videos on !Nvite. [Silence 0.5]Kid had a plastic Halloween mask over his face-- a skull... [Silence 0.5]but like the worst dollar-store skull you could find. [Silence 0.5]You could see his eyes through it - big no-no when it comes to avoiding a profiler. [Silence 0.5]He had distorted his voice, but didn't change his speech patterns.

The Wrench... man... what to say about this guy? [Silence 0.1]Some freaky shit going on right there. [Silence 0.1]I'd like to say he's actually a sensitive, charming guy beneath the harsh exterior, [Silence 0.1]but I'm pretty sure he’s a "fucked up motherfucker" all the way through. [Silence 0.1]I don't even know who first recruited him, he just started showing up at local hackerspaces and building his "tools of destruction." [Silence 0.1]At first I thought he was trying too hard... [Silence 0.1]like he was a FBI plant or something... [Silence 0.1]but no agent's going to pull the kind of suicidal stunts this guy does. I think the truth is... Wrench doesn't care if he dies, but he's not going quietly.

Now, if there was a spectrum spanning anarchist to activist, we'd probably fill the whole damn thing. [Silence 0.1]But there is one thing that unites the key crew--each one of us has a reason to hate big data, or more specifically, [Silence 0.1]Blume and its "ctOS." [Silence 0.1]I've been overseeing operations... making sure people get where they need to be with the tools they require. [Silence 0.1]I've got eyes on the big picture. [Silence 0.1]The way I see it, I've lit the fuse. [Silence 0.1]It's only a matter of time before Blume feels the DedSec explosion.

See Josh, he's high-functioning autistic--which means he's got a very specific way of talking. [Silence 0.1]Sitara found him easily, but he wasn't at all what we expected. [Silence 0.1]When you get down to pure coding, Josh operates on a higher level than the rest of us. [Silence 0.1]We got a look at his ctOS profile and all kinds of nasty flags popped up. [Silence 0.1]"Emotionally challenged," "unstable," even a low "mental maturity" score. [Silence 0.1]He is none of those things and he quickly become the activist soul of our group. [Silence 0.1]He has a black and white way of seeing things, fair and unfair, which means he can be refreshing and often hilarious. [Silence 0.5]We caught a glimpse of the damage the ctOS dealt him: rejected care programs, cut funding... overcharges. [Silence 0.1]We offered to help him make things right.

When we met Josh, he had the right intentions and the wrong approach-like a laser putting on a pretty lightshow instead of burning holes. [Silence 0.1]If Blume's system wants to make him unemployable, damn straight we're going to snatch him up and point him right back at 'em.

Even so... I'm glad we've got the Wrench on our side. [Silence 0.1]One of the group's biggest problems is a lack of GSD... [Silence 0.1]Gettin' Shit Done. [Silence 0.1]The Wrench is pure GSD and he brings his own sledgehammer. [Silence 0.1]He's not some dumb thug, either... [Silence 0.1]I've seen some of his code--he's legit. [Silence 0.1]Probably why he's interested in DedSec and not some street gang. [Silence 0.5]You know what, I take that back. [Silence 0.1]He might actually belong to a street gang. Who knows.

One thing I do know about Wrench... the man hates Blume. [Silence 0.1]I mean HATES them. [Silence 0.1]I can't get the "why" from him. [Silence 0.1]It's obvious he wears the mask to avoid facial recognition, [Silence 0.1]but what's he hiding FROM? He's not saying.

Let's talk about Sitara. She's been driving DedSec in the Bay Area. [Silence 0.1]The Hackerspace? She's paying for it with... "borrowed" money. Every DedSec poster, every flyer? That's Sitara. She's even had a hand in our core toolset-- found one of the first Zero Days in ctOS 2.0. Some of the guys call her "Madame President," but I see her as more of a pirate captain. She'll lead you to the treasure, but you piss her off, you're walking the plank.

I had a long talk with her once. [Silence 0.1]Found out where she gets her relentless drive. [Silence 0.1]She's got rich parents back home in Kolkata, and I mean drive-a-car-in-the-house rich. [Silence 0.5]They sent her to ivy league schools (yes, plural) hoping to expand the dynasty, I suppose. [Silence 0.5]But she didn't stick with it. She rejected their money, too, everything she's got now was taken from people she says "didn't deserve it."

Sitara's seen her own relatives pulling strings, taking advantage. [Silence 0.1]She says shit like that will never change because the people at the bottom think they can't change it. [Silence 0.5]And she says we're right at the heart of it now... with Silicon Valley pushing us towards the point of no return. [Silence 0.1]Replacing elite individuals with unstoppable corporations. [Silence 0.1]Blume makes the top of her hit-list and she calls ctOS 2.0 their preemptive strike on any opposition.

So we've been looking at this new guy... calls himself Retr0. [Silence 0.1]Now, I like his style. Spent some time in Oakland... in fact, that's where he earned some of his hacker cred. [Silence 0.1]I read everything I could about him when it was going down - the Home Domain Center had a deal with Homeland Security. [Silence 0.1]They rolled out cameras into Oakland and started stockpiling data on everybody. [Silence 0.1]Somehow Retr0 got targeted by the thing--it profiled him based on his computer skills and marked him as the prime suspect in a local high-tech robbery. [Silence 0.1]The evidence was all digital... nothing put him at that crime scene. [Silence 0.1]And the case? Was a shitshow - full of quotes from people who didn't know anything about technology. [Silence 0.1]Lies everywhere. False flags and fear-mongering. [Silence 0.1]They weren't about to admit to a flaw in their system.

Retr0 got lucky. [Silence 0.1]He got a judge that decided not to throw the book at him. [Silence 0.1]So he ended up with community service. [Silence 0.1]He says it wasn't a big deal 'cause he got to work with kids. [Silence 0.1]Taught them the truth about the systems in place. [Silence 0.1]Probably the best lesson they ever learned. [Silence 0.1]But he knew he was going back after the HDC. [Silence 0.1]He data-mined them. Hacked into accounts of their key members. [Silence 0.1]Exposed every little thing that showed just how corrupt the system was. [Silence 0.1]A huge victory, right? [Silence 0.1]Yeah, maybe not so much. Oh, he spanked the HDC, no question. [Silence 0.1]Got the program shut down hard. [Silence 0.1]So where did all those cameras in Oakland go? [Silence 0.1]They're still there, but guess who owns them now? [Silence 0.1]Blume. They're part of the ctOS. [Silence 0.1]Being used to track and profile people, just like the HDC was doing. [Silence 0.1]And now Retr0's got himself a nasty profile on record. [Silence 0.1]We think he's going to be eager to do something about it and I can't wait to see him work. [Silence 0.1]My bet--he's prime DedSec material.
If I've got to drag their asses out to the middle of the desert to keep DedSec together, I'm going to do it. DedSec's come too far to give up now.
People. Our desert assignment: get fucking wasted. Fuck shit up. Chill the fuck out. DedSec will come back stronger when the smoke clears.
Man... this is it. Part of something huge now. DedSec's gonna help me get back at Blume.
But first.... pants. Pants are important.
What the fuck. Why's my threat so high?
Scheduled traffic stop? Man, they're stalking me...
Income goes up, threat goes down. Of course.

How many are actually giving us access to their computers?
All of them. That's the whole point. They give us access to their power, we grow a network of computers that makes us stronger--our own giant cloud computing network.
So do people sign a contract? "I vow to let DedSec own my processor?"
We're transparent. They know before they ever install the app that they're giving us access to their computing power... but never their personal info.
That's a lot of trust. Silicon Valley would kill to have that level of intrusion. Private data farming runs their whole economy.
But we look out for our own, man. That’s why people are joining our movement. To make a statement against the technocrats.
Marcus... have you looked at our follower count lately?

We've got to make people see Blume for what it is, Marcus. The longer it takes, the more they rely on ctOS... they'll get used to things the way they are. And then DedSec becomes the conspiracy theory fringe. It won't matter if what we're saying is true if people don't want it to be.
Yeah... but this is just the start. When we show them the shit that's brewing behind Blume's doors, they'll join us in droves.
The RC speed boost is useful in Drone Races, where speed is of the essence.

That's going to get a reaction from Blume. I can't believe people let them grab so much power. All that sci-fi shit we read as kids... big brother, thought control, pre-crime. It's all here now, isn't it? Thanks to Blume and their ctOS. Those authors saw it coming decades ago, but nobody listened. Everybody's too sold on pleasant corporate platitudes and flawless branding to realize the whole damn thing's a societal trojan.

In other cities, when it was still ctOS 1.0... we had a lot. Sucks because we were too careless. Missed our window to do something big. And 2.0... we're the first group to go up against it, so we're still playing catch-up. They were expecting us this time.
The thought of DedSec written on a whiteboard in some Blume office makes me all squishy inside.
We keep it up, next time maybe they'll use the red marker.
Marcus, our followers network is becoming a steamroller.

You should be proud--you started all of this. DedSec was a bunch of loose ideas before, but you've turned it into a movement. People are wearing your art. Repeating your slogans. You've tuned into something here.
Thank you Marcus. [beat]Just don't forget, there's purpose behind this. I'm not in it for the candy coating. I want people to wake the fuck up.
They've been sleeping a long time, but they'll get there.
THIS IS IT. We're fucking there. We've leaked all of Dusan's lies. The backroom deals. He is going down hard.
Malware, exploits, and potential delivery systems?
Oh, we are SO going to do that.

It doesn't help that ctOS actually does what they say it does, either. We're opposing a system that helps people on the surface, but exploits them behind the scenes. Makes it easy to paint us as the bad guys.
Question for you... how much access does DedSec have to ctOS?

Fine, fine. I'm just trying to find the mobile clinic.
Listen, you may be stupid, but no one deserves that. Don't go to the clinic.
I just want to find out more about it.
They trick people into free healthcare, inject us with tiny machines, and watch to see if we live or die. There, you know it all!
That was... a lot of information.
I know it sounds crazy. The Police didn't believe me, either. But the clinic staff... they heard me. [scared]And now they're trying to kill me.
That why you're hiding out in the batcave?
Duh. If anyone asks, you didn't see me.
Huh. I wish I knew what I was seeing...
It feels like I'm in a cyperpunk sci-fi movie.
I know how to hurt them. We burn their shit to the ground, baby.
Ok, that's... that's one way to do it...
No no no, that's the only way to do it, alright. Fast and mean. This one's mine, Marcus. Marcus, don't you fucking sideline me on this one, bud. Ok, this one's mine.
Alright, alright. Fine. We do it Wrench-style. What do you need?
Alright, ok well Sitara linked a bunch of house sales to the one guy--Bratva royalty.
So you... you literally want to burn that shit to the ground?
I'm just a naughty little noobie, waiting for the NSA to penetrate my ports.
Citizens of the world, are you ready for DedSexxx? [Silence 2]
DedSec has learned of mysterious deaths among the homeless, possibly caused by illegal experiments.
Time to investigate the mobile clinics and find out exactly what they're doing.
Meet DedSec scout at the water tower
We're breaking into RenSense, stopping their experiments, and saving their victims.
Unlock the door to the lab
Find the injection gun in a yellow barrel
Find the clues by using NetHack
Malicious hackers have crippled Bay Area hospitals with ransomware. DedSec's regrouping at the Hackerspace to brainstorm ideas on how to shut it down.
DedSec has tracked the hospital ransomware infection point back to Streamer's rented servers. If we can discover the infection point, we should be able to track it back to the source.
We've tracked the source of the ransomware infection to a private cell phone. Finding that phone gets DedSec one step closer to finding a solution.
DedSec now has a trail to follow, but with a possible hitman on our heels and a clear link between the ransomware and the Russian mafia, this operation could quickly go south.
Talk to Josh at the Hackerspace
Drive to the Bratva server location
Download details on the ransomware operation
We've tracked Anton to his luxury yacht just offshore. He'll have the ransomware key onboard, but we can count on it being highly secured. Time to get creative.
Alejandro Jackofski has made a mockery of the DedSec name in his latest porn movie, which is flattering, but he also happens to be an abusive asshole. We're going to teach him a lesson.
Meet Sitara in the pawn shop
DedSec's plan to humiliate Alejandro Jackofski went off without a hitch. Now, we celebrate. We're gathering up at the Hackerspace. Come join us!
Hack the car crusher to stop it
The Bratva abducted and tried to murder one of our own. We will not stand for it. We're headed to the war room and you can bet the Bratva are going to answer for their actions.
The Bratva has waged war on us, attacking our members and our reputation on multiple fronts. We will not stand for it. Join us as we retaliate.
All of our efforts to fight back against the Bratva culminate in this final attack on their finances, their personal property, and their morale. And don't forget to stay for the fireworks at the end.
Meet with DedSec on the sailboat
Pay tribute to the Rat with this stylish custom suit.
Show off your gamer cred with this Twitch Hoodie
Select the Nudle Engineer Mission using the Driver: SF App
Marcus, when you're free, we should talk.
I hate that question. Something is always wrong. It's a stupid question.
Wrench, you need to air out your mask once in a while. Find some peace.
Err no, that's the opposite of what I need to do. The mask keeps me calm, Marcus.

So until we have this ransomware key, what's the damage we're looking at? Off the top of my head... access to patient records, patient tracking, lab results... can't they switch back to paper backups? They're supposed to keep them.
They do, but it slows everything down to the point that you're going to want to pay the ransomers to avoid the trouble.
[Sigh] Now, what hospital's going to pay up? You do it once, you can expect to be held for ransom every year after.

Several hospitals paid up in the past--thousands of dollars, too. Some of them did get their systems back... probably infested with malware. In one case they paid up, but the ransomers just took the money and ran.
Motherfuckers. Nothing worse than a dishonest crook. That's just bad for business.
Paper backups don't factor in reliance on software to analyze scan results.
Nor do they let you coordinate those results with experts in other cities or countries.
Yeah, I gotcha, Josh. So our only option is to find that ransomware key. Let's hope they've left a trail at Streamer.
"DedSec Saves Bay Area Hospitals" looks real good on the resumé.
Ok... I'm inside the Streamer building. I'll see if I can get you all access to the servers.
Oh, can you set me up with a free account while you're in there?
Download the data before the rival team
True, but I've never been a V.I.P. of anything before.
Violent, Irritating Pervert? Yeah, mine too.
People, you are now free to snoop through Streamer's servers. They have several that start with "MED."
They didn't even try to hide them. No wonder they got hacked. Here it is... I see Pl0xy installed on all the MED servers two weeks ago.
Guys, I've found the link - definitely Bratva... but there was a complication.
Can you track it to the source device?
Hold on... yes. We've got GPS coordinates. Looks like a phone.
Send them to me. I'll check it out.
Marcus, you need to listen to this...

Bay area hospitals struggle to maintain service as their computers are crippled by ransomware. Hospital officials claim there are delays, but they are keeping up care despite the setback. However, inside sources tell us paying the ransom is now under heavy consideration.
If they pay out, this operation's a bust. Let's hope we find something soon.
I'll post something from DedSec so they know we're on it. They won't acknowledge it publicly, but maybe it will be enough to stall their decision.
About six feet tall. Chinese. Wears a designer suit when he's out murdering people.
Sounds like you stepped in a big ole' pile of organized crime drama. Could be a Shu hitman.
Hitman sounds about right, but I don't think he's Shu. I gave him the slip, but he's after the same people we are.
You couldn't get him to work with us?
Ah, sanity's never been a prerequisite.
I'm headed back to the hackerspace. Let's see what we can dig up with the new info.

You know what... you have really inconvenienced me, kid. Bad enough I gotta take a red eye out to this hipster shithole and deal with some serious humidity issues--I mean what the fuck--sweating balls in the morning and freezing them at night... where the hell was I?

Right... you're an inconvenience. Now you've got me way off my path. Talking to goddamn nerds, or geeks, or whatever the fuck you want to identify with. You know what, we'll go with dorks. And not just dorks, now I'm wasting my time working with some kind of "woke" dork activists. Am I using that word right? Woke?
Anyway, couple years back I would have popped two in your face for just seeing mine. Something's wrong with me. Going to have to see my guy about that.
Just focus on the task at hand and maybe you survive this shit. Maybe.
Sorry, pal. This is going to sting a little.
Sometimes I like to pretend the bullets are like little cats chasing after my laser pointer.
This one's got a little something on his face. I'm going to help him with that.
This guy has the dumbest look on his face and it's pissing me off... you have no idea.
Ok... I see what you're doing here. Just have to think it through.
Looks like the Bratva's running an operation at the Crystal Springs dam.
Funny, I thought you'd say Pier 13.
No shit? Huh. So where's Anton?
Looks like these guys are tapping into the data lines reserved for the hospitals. The ransomware's probably just a distraction to keep eyes off the data theft.
You could resell that data for millions. A lot more than they'll get to unlock the system.
A backup of all the data's being sent to a luxury yacht. My guess - it's his.
Fuck me. I know the one. I was going to blow it up to intimidate the Bratva.
Don't blow it up. I need what's on it.
Yeah, well if Anton's onboard, I need to make a-- an example... up close and personal. [beat] You know what... meet me outside. Sending you the coordinates.
I've tracked the Bratva hacker, Anton, to a fancy yacht.
Wait... Bratva hackers get a yacht? We don't even have a bathroom. We literally have to go and pee in the alley.
You guys better not be pissing on my artwork.
Well, just paint it up high and you won't have to worry about any splash damage.
Thanks for drawing fire away from me. I owe you one.
That was fun. You're a fun guy, you know?
Yeah? Why don't you stick around and play some more?
No can do... playdate with Anton. Toodles.
I think I gotta check out Lenni's info on the homeless deaths.
It doesn't hurt to check it out.
Nanotech... Fuck! Lenni may be right.
Oh, nice. They've got a sniper too. Dueling snipers.
I see you, Mr. Sniper Scope. Do you see me?
Bad news for you. Looks like their friends have shown up for the party.
There, let me create a little distraction for you...
Might want to keep your head down.
That's what I like to see.
Dum dum dum dum dum dum dum dum.
Somebody could really get hurt out here.
Are you trying to piss me off?
And the batter strikes out. Too bad.
Did you see the preview yet? It looks good. A little irritating they didn't give more personality to the enemy AI. All they do is stand around and bitch about bullshit like long hours and bad pay.
Or brag about killing people, yeah. I'd love to hear them complain about real life shit for a change. What are these guys into? What movies do they watch? What games do they play?
Maybe we should go down to the dev studio and voice our opinions... if you know what I mean.
That's a long road trip. I don't get paid enough for road trips.
